audit.why: Melee-locked scaling carry: Riven owns Levels 1-3 outright, Levels 4-5 are contested while Kayle farms toward her range breakpoint, and everything from 6 onward belongs to Kayle. 51.1% over 1086 games is the razor-thin number you would expect from a lane that is won early and lost late.
audit.corrected: No change needed to diff/diffRating; the 4/10 difficulty with a 9.5/10 carry threat is the right shape.

audit.whatIsWrong: The last four chart rows were wrong in both layers. The page read Riven / Skill / Riven / Riven for Levels 4-5, Level 6, First item and 2+ items, against a packet chart of Skill / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle — and the whys underneath already argued Kayle's case ('she is stronger in extended fights than you are at this stage', 'nearly impossible to kill in a straight duel') while the side said Riven.
audit.why: Kayle goes ranged on Divine Ascent at 6 and her item spikes are the whole point of the champion. A page that tells a Riven player she still wins the First item and 2+ item rows is telling her to take the fight that loses the game. The mirror resolved the same four rows the same way.
audit.corrected: Proposed as the whole chart group in matched full/content pairs: phases[3].side + win[3] -> Skill, phases[4].side + win[4] -> Kayle, phases[5].side + win[5] -> Kayle, phases[6].side + win[6] -> Kayle, with ratings walked down 5/10, 4/10, 3/10, 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page credits Kayle's ranged transformation to Starfire Spellblade (E) in whys[4], mid and wants.foe[1]. The range comes from Divine Ascent (P) — 'progressively gains Attack Speed, Move Speed, Attack Range' as she levels. Starfire Spellblade is an auto-attack reset dealing bonus damage scaled to missing health, on a 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s cooldown. Divine Judgment is also described only as 'her get-out at 6' with no cooldown, when it is 160/120/80s and 900 range — it can be spent on an ally, which changes whether it is available for her.
audit.why: A player told the E is what makes her ranged will try to bait the E and walk in, and get kited by a passive that has no cooldown to bait. The real punish trigger is her Radiant Blast: 900 range, 12/11/10/9/8s, and it shreds resistances on the way in — commit while it is spent, not while E is spent.
audit.corrected: Divine Ascent named as the range source in whys[4] and wants.foe[1]; Starfire Spellblade correctly described as the ~8s auto reset; Radiant Blast's 900 range and 12-to-8s cooldown written into whys[3]; Divine Judgment's 160/120/80s cooldown, 900 range and ally-targeting written into dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t tells the player to buy Executioner's Calling early because 'his healing fights your pattern' — wrong pronoun and no mechanism named.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal for Celestial Blessing. It is a flat 15s cooldown heal with no rank scaling on the cooldown, so in a long lane she gets it back roughly every other wave — that is what decides extended trades, and the item line should say so.
audit.corrected: Named the ability and the 15s cooldown in report[8].t, and put the same fact into whys[3] where the player is deciding whether to commit.
